1.name: tier 1
1.lattices: the axis plus one or two non-rational classes with lcm <= 180, saturated (every unit vector of the lattice a generator)
1.odd_girth: FS-58's odd_girth, exact to length 15 or a 400,000-point BFS cap, whichever binds first; none_up_to recorded

1b.name: tier 1b (the radius ladder)
1b.defined: 2026-09-20, plans/FS61-quadratic-census.md, the owner's re-plan after phase B, ruling 2 (phase B')
1b.scope: every rank-4 lattice whose state is Open and whose tier-1 R = 1.5 ball record is `Over cap (not asked)`; a lattice whose R = 1.5 ball was asked is out of scope, and tier 1's definition is unchanged
1b.lattices: tier 1's lattices, unchanged: the axis plus one or two non-rational classes with lcm <= 180, saturated
1b.odd_girth: tier 1's, unchanged; no lattice record is rewritten by this tier
1b.radius_rule: walk the rungs 1.2 then 1.0. A rung whose PREDICTED points (pi^2 R^4 / covolume) exceed point_cap is not asked; the first rung whose prediction fits is asked. If that rung's EXACT point count also exceeds point_cap the ladder descends to the next fitting rung -- the exact count is strictly better information than the prediction and the descent can only ask more, never fewer. If no rung's prediction fits, one `Over cap (not asked)` record is written at the first rung carrying both predictions.
1b.onset_rule: a rung that refuses is followed by the next rung down at a 120 s wall, as phase B's onset radii were, to hand phase C a smaller refusing ball; it is a bonus ask and never part of the accounting

2.name: tier 2
2.defined: 2026-09-19, plans/FS61-quadratic-census.md decision B (phase E; d = 7 mod 8 fields not landed at tier 1, 167 excluded)
2.lattices: the axis plus one or two non-rational classes with lcm <= 420, saturated
2.odd_girth: FS-58's odd_girth, exact to length 15 or a 400,000-point BFS cap, whichever binds first; none_up_to recorded

1c.name: tier 1c (the degree-targeted ask)
1c.defined: 2026-09-20, the owner's revision of E.1a, on his measurement that what separates a decided ball from an undecided one is its AVERAGE DEGREE and not its size. Minted and then redefined the same hour, before any record carried it: the first definition re-asked tier 1b's undecided balls at a longer wall, and six of those fourteen sat at average degree 5.51, below the 6.595 at which any ball has ever refused.
1c.scope: every rank-4 lattice whose state is `Open` or `Refused` at a census field with no certified witness -- one uniform rule over all 31 such fields, 167 included under it like every other. A lattice's ask is decided by the degree rule below and not by which radii an earlier tier happened to reach.
1c.lattices: tier 1's lattices, unchanged; this tier creates no lattice record
1c.degree_law: a ball of radius R on a lattice holding g unit vectors has predicted average degree g*phi(R)^2, where phi(R) = [2R^2*acos(1/(2R)) - sqrt(4R^2-1)/2] / (pi*R^2) is the area fraction a radius-R disc shares with its unit translate, squared because a ball here is a bidisc -- one disc per real embedding. Control over the 734 asked ball records carrying points and edges: observed/predicted has median 1.0000 and range 0.715-1.184, with 0 outside +-30%.
1c.radius_rule: ask ONE ball per lattice. Arm `R14`: the radius where the predicted degree is 14, if its predicted points fit the point cap -- 43 of 43 recorded balls of at least 200,000 points at degree >= 14 decided, none undecided. Arm `Rcap`: otherwise the largest radius whose predicted points fit the cap, provided its predicted degree is at least the floor of 8. Arm `overcap`: otherwise no ask, and the record carries the predicted degree at the cap, which is the honest answer to `what would deepen this row`. A lattice already DECIDED at a radius at or above the rule's target is not re-asked, and its record says so.

1u.name: tier 1u (the certification-onset ask: upward in degree, on a lattice that already refuses)
1u.defined: 2026-09-20, the owner's acceptance of FS-61's certification pass. At d = 239 the refusing ball sits at average degree 14.0, refuses in 403 s, and collapses slowly under extraction (369,885 -> 46,338 points in core round 0; 8,336 points after 52 rounds, heading for a certificate of hundreds of megabytes). The census's own degree phase diagram is therefore turned on the CERTIFICATE rather than on the refusal: on a fixed lattice a denser ball refuses FASTER and collapses FURTHER (d = 47: 104 s at R = 1.2, under a second at 1.5; d = 311: 1,137,169 points at degree 14 refused in 18 s and core round 0 left 738 of them).
1u.purpose: a cheaper CERTIFICATE SOURCE, never a new refusal. Refusal is monotone in radius -- balls about one centre on one lattice are nested -- so a larger ball of a refusing lattice refuses too, and no ask of this tier can change a field's census state. What it asks is how fast that larger ball refuses and how far the first extraction round collapses it.
1u.scope: every lattice carrying a `Refused` ball record at a census field with NO certified witness -- refusing but uncertified. A lattice with no `Refused` record is REFUSED an ask by the rule, and so is every lattice at a field already `Landed (certified)`. This tier creates no lattice record.
1u.lattices: none of its own: it re-asks lattices earlier tiers built, at whatever NMAX built them
1u.degree_law: tier 1c's, unchanged: predicted average degree is g*phi(R)^2 with phi(R) = [2R^2*acos(1/(2R)) - sqrt(4R^2-1)/2] / (pi*R^2), the area fraction a radius-R disc shares with its unit translate, squared because a ball here is a bidisc.
1u.radius_rule: ask ONE ball per in-scope lattice. Arm `R18`: the radius where the predicted degree reaches 18, if its predicted points fit the point cap divided by the 1.11 overshoot margin tier 1c measured. Arm `Rcap`: otherwise the largest radius whose predicted points fit that margin. THE ASK MUST RAISE THE DEGREE -- an arm whose predicted degree does not strictly exceed the predicted degree of the refusing ball it is aimed at is refused, and the record reads `No lift (not asked)` carrying both degrees. This tier exists to move UP the phase diagram; a lower-degree ball of the same lattice is a step toward the hardness peak at degree 4-6, where no ball has ever refused. Because degree rises with radius at a fixed generator count, a lifting ask is automatically at a strictly larger radius than the refusing ball, which is what makes its refusal free by nesting.

2l.name: tier 2l (deeper lattices, the same degree rule)
2l.defined: 2026-09-20, the owner's re-plan after phase B' ruling 3 item E.1b, as revised the same day: `E.1b keeps its pricing rule and uses this same ask rule in place of the ladder`.
2l.scope: every census field with no certified witness. Lattices to NMAX = 420 -- a superset of tier 1's NMAX = 180 set, so every earlier tier's ball record still answers the ball it answered and is never re-asked; the new work is the finer lattices. The ask rule, the point cap and the solver's wall are tier 1c's: this tier buys DEPTH, and tier 1c bought DEGREE.
2l.lattices: the axis plus one or two non-rational classes with lcm <= 420, saturated (every unit vector of the lattice a generator)
2l.odd_girth: NOT computed at this tier: every 2l lattice record carries odd_girth.status `not asked`. Phase 0 measured the exact odd girth at about 900x the cost of the rest of `lattices` (1,648 CPU-s against 1.8 s at d = 11), and R-cycle is scored on tier 1's lattices, whose population is stated. A 2l lattice has no odd-girth column and must not be counted in an odd-girth table.
2l.degree_law: tier 1c's, unchanged: predicted average degree is g*phi(R)^2 with phi the disc/unit-translate overlap fraction, squared for the bidisc.
2l.radius_rule: tier 1c's, unchanged: one ball per lattice, at the radius where the predicted degree reaches 14 if its predicted points fit the cap (with the same margin below it), else the largest radius under the cap whose predicted degree is at least 8, else an `Over cap (not asked)` record carrying the degree it would reach at the cap.
